output.company: Carvana Co. (NYSE: CVNA), consolidated; assessment as of 2026-10-21

ownership.value: Publicly listed, Garcia-family controlled. The 2025 Form 10-K states that the Garcia Parties held approximately 83% of voting power at December 31, 2025. The June 2026 Form 10-Q continues to describe their ten-vote Class B rights, subject to the ownership threshold; no recent change of control was verified.

debt_events.summary: Entered a $1.66 billion senior secured Term Loan B, due 2033-08-14, issued at 99.75; interest at Term SOFR plus 2.25% or base rate plus 1.25%. Proceeds were designated to refinance all 2030 secured notes, with redemptions scheduled for August 15 and 22. Quarterly amortization is 0.25% of original principal beginning with the second full fiscal quarter after closing. This filing documents a refinancing, not a distressed exchange.

Management estimated the refinancing would reduce annual cash interest by approximately $45 million over the next four years on a leverage-neutral basis; this is a company estimate, not realized savings.

Company reported compliance with all debt covenants. Note 9 reports $319 million current debt principal, excluding finance leases, and $32 million of unsecured notes due April 15, 2027. Reviewed current filings did not establish a new missed payment, bankruptcy or distressed exchange; this is not a comprehensive legal clearance.

Added a $500 million finance-receivable revolving facility through November 8, 2027. March 2026 amendment increased another facility to $600 million and extended maturity to June 30, 2027. At June 30, aggregate finance-receivable facilities had $4.1 billion unused capacity, but collateral-based immediately available borrowing is lower than nominal unused commitments.

Historical notes exchange: the June 2026 filing identifies September 2023 exchange offers and the resulting senior secured debt. This is historical liability-management context, not a new event in the last 12 months.

credit_ratings.summary: S&P affirmed issuer credit rating BB-, outlook Positive; senior secured issue rating upgraded to BB from BB-, senior unsecured rating affirmed at B. Latest opened issuer action identified through 2026-10-21.

Moody’s upgraded long-term foreign-currency rating to B1 from B2, outlook Positive, as reported by Cbonds on 2026-06-25. Latest opened Moody’s action identified through 2026-10-21; primary agency action text was not available.

Fitch assigned a first-time long-term issuer default rating of BB-. The opened entity page confirms rating, action and date but does not populate the outlook; outlook is unverified. Latest opened issuer action identified through 2026-10-21.

output.risk_rationale: As of 2026-10-21, Carvana has elevated rather than acute credit risk: its ratings remain speculative grade, and June 2026 reported debt of $5.133 billion excludes finance leases and sits alongside substantial secured financing and a $2.130 billion tax-receivable-agreement liability ([10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1690820/000169082026000055/cvna-20260630.htm); [S&P](https://spratings.spglobal.com/ratings/en/regulatory/article/-/view/sourceId/101672419)). Near-term debt-service capacity is supported by $2.630 billion cash, $4.669 billion committed liquidity resources, positive operating cash flow, covenant compliance and the August refinancing, but the broader $7.024 billion liquidity figure includes conditional debt capacity rather than only immediately available funding ([10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1690820/000169082026000055/cvna-20260630.htm); [8-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1690820/000169082026000059/cvna-20260814.htm)). Counterparty exposure also includes documented historical seller-payment and loan-payoff delays, so liquidity improvement should not be treated as assurance of flawless operational performance ([Connecticut Attorney General](https://portal.ct.gov/ag/press-releases/2025-press-releases/attorney-general-tong-announces-settlement-with-carvana-following-hundreds-of-consumer-complaints)).

distress_signals.summary: June 30 Form 10-Q: management stated that working capital, operating cash flow and expected continued or new financing arrangements should fund operations for at least one year from financial-statement issuance. This is conditional management guidance, not a cash-only runway estimate.

Accrual for unresolved legal matters was $10 million, versus $14 million at December 31, 2025. Filing warns that unfavorable developments could materially affect business, results, financial condition or cash flows; unresolved claims are not adjudicated payment defaults.

2025 annual audit: Grant Thornton LLP reported an unqualified financial-statement opinion and effective internal control over financial reporting; it stated it had served as auditor since 2015. No going-concern qualification was identified in the opened annual audit report.
Company scheduled Q3 2026 results for October 28, after the assessment cutoff. Accordingly, the latest available quarterly financials used here are for June 30, not September 30.

payment_behaviour.summary: Connecticut Attorney General announced a $1.5 million settlement following hundreds of consumer complaints, including delayed seller payments, delayed loan payoffs and title/registration delays. Terms included $1 million restitution and a $500,000 penalty, with $250,000 suspended if conditions were met. Investigation began in January 2022; this is historical customer/seller obligation evidence, not proof of current supplier arrears.
